title: No Unsafe Needed
goal: Turn a u32 into its little-endian bytes. One version uses unsafe that std makes unnecessary.
hints: Before transmuting, search the type's methods - integers know how to serialize themselves.
The hand-rolled loop is safe and correct. It's also a reimplementation of a one-line std call.
explanation: All three produce identical bytes. transmute is the heaviest tool in the language - here it signs an unsafe waiver for something `u32::to_le_bytes()` does safely, in one call, with the endianness in the name. The hand-rolled loop avoids unsafe but rebuilds std with mutable state and shift arithmetic to review. The instinct this trains: most unsafe (and most clever bit-twiddling) in application code is a std method you haven't found yet. Look first.
